presentation.title: Water-based strawberry bars surge +38.2% while chocolate-coated lines ease -4.6%
presentation.html:
Main observations

All 4 Districts · 4 SKUs

Value price · Strawberry · Water-based

+38.2% Recent vs forecast: +44.6% · Fill rate: 88.2%

Replenishment requests for refreshing value strawberry water ice bars surged to 15,785 units against 10,912.7 expected over the past 14 days. The surge outpaced warehouse shipments, leaving 1,859 unfilled store units across all 20 outlets.

All 4 Districts · 10 SKUs

Other chocolate-coated

-4.6% Recent vs forecast: -5.7% · Fill rate: 99.3%

Chocolate-coated items softened steadily across all 4 districts to 23,595 units against 25,029.5 expected. The reduction is widespread across cones and crunch bars, while store fulfillment remained near-perfect at 99.3%.

Store replenishment patterns show a clear divergence: stores are shifting demand toward light, thirst-quenching water ice bars while heavier chocolate-coated lines cool off, requiring rebalancing of forward inventory.

Secondary observations

All 4 Districts · 3 SKUs

Other value price · Strawberry (Creamy)

+0.2% Recent vs forecast: -0.6% · 14-day requests: 6,345

Unlike water-based bars, creamy strawberry value lines (such as Strawberry Cream and Milk Ice Bars) tracked expected demand closely at 6,345 units versus 6,383.8 expected, confirming that the uplift is driven by refreshing format rather than strawberry flavor alone.

Action recommendations

Purchasing adjustments result in a net increase of 95 cases (+1.5 pallets footprint). Whole-warehouse peak capacity is projected at 61.3 pallets against the 66.0 pallet limit (0.0 pallets excess), safely accommodating these orders.

questions.text: Did regional stores report any localized end-cap displays or outdoor marketing initiatives driving the sharp replenishment surge in water-based strawberry bars?
Do merchandisers anticipate chocolate-coated demand stabilizing as school holidays progress, or should we plan for extended softness into August?

args.report:
Weekly purchasing review for week starting 2026-07-27.

1. Main Observations:
- Value price, water-based strawberry bars have experienced an estimated sustained demand uplift of +38.2% across all 4 districts. Over the past 14 days, stores requested 15,785 units against 10,912.7 expected (+44.6% raw deviation). Replenishment demand outpaced distribution capacity, leading to an 88.2% fill rate and 1,859 unfilled store units across all 20 outlets.
- Chocolate-coated products have softened across the network with an estimated sustained change of -4.6% (-5.7% raw deviation over the last 14 days; 23,595 requested units vs 25,029.5 expected). Fulfillment remained solid at 99.3%, indicating that store demand itself cooled across cones and crunch bars.

2. Secondary Observations:
- Within value strawberry lines, the surge is concentrated exclusively in water-based refreshment formats. Dairy-based value strawberry bars remained flat (+0.2% estimated sustained change; -0.6% raw deviation), confirming that customer preferences have pivoted toward lighter, thirst-quenching bars rather than a category-wide strawberry affinity.

3. Action Recommendations:
- Value price · Strawberry · Water-based: Increase purchase orders sharply by 132 cases (+2.2 pallets footprint), including boosting Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar (IC062) by 54 cases and Strawberry Breeze Ice Bar (IC063) by 36 cases, to restore store service levels and capture HK$16,114 in avoided lost margin.
- Other chocolate-coated: Reduce purchase orders slightly by 37 cases (-0.7 pallets footprint) across 10 SKUs, led by reductions in Coffee Crunch Bar (IC046, -7 cases) and Double Choc Cone (IC018, -6 cases), aligning stock with lower demand.
- Warehouse physical capacity comfortably absorbs these changes, projecting peak warehouse occupancy at 61.3 pallets against the 66.0 pallet ceiling (0.0 pallet excess).

claims.text: Value price strawberry water-based ice bars experienced an estimated sustained demand uplift of 38.2% (80% CI: 35.1% to 41.3%), with recent 14-day requests reaching 15,785 units against 10,912.7 expected (+44.6% raw deviation) across all 20 stores.

Warehouse fulfillment for value strawberry water-based bars achieved an 88.2% fill rate over the past 14 days, shipping 13,926 of 15,785 requested units, with 1,859 unfilled store requests and 153 open cases arriving through 31 July.

Increase purchasing orders for value price strawberry water-based bars by 132 cases (+2.2 pallets footprint), lifting representative SKU IC062 (Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar) from 46 to 100 cases, to recover store service levels and capture an estimated HK$16,114 in avoided lost margin.

Chocolate-coated products softened across all districts with an estimated sustained change of -4.6% (80% CI: -6.0% to -3.2%), recording 23,595 requested units against 25,029.5 expected (-5.7% raw deviation) and an intact 99.3% fulfillment rate.

Reduce purchasing orders for chocolate-coated products by 37 cases (-0.7 pallets footprint) across 10 SKUs, including trimming Coffee Crunch Bar (IC046) by 7 cases and Double Choc Cone (IC018) by 6 cases, aligning replenishments to slower demand.

The demand surge in strawberry is concentrated specifically in refreshing water-based value formats rather than dairy-based varieties, as other value strawberry items remained essentially flat (+0.2% estimated effect, -0.6% raw deviation), indicating a consumer preference shift toward lighter refreshment during high summer.

Total projected warehouse peak capacity utilization stands at 61.3 pallets against the 66.0 pallet warehouse ceiling (inherited peak also at 61.3 pallets), leaving 0.0 pallets physical capacity excess and fully accommodating the net +1.5 pallet purchase expansion.

result.group_rule: Catalog groups use the existing tag and frozen numeric-band definitions; intersections are AND.

sample.rule: At least 3 products, 7 observed days, 100 requested units and 95% expected-row coverage; this is an adequacy heuristic.

result.prior_year_basis: Same calendar dates one year earlier, same products and districts; not weather-adjusted.

shift_share.basis: Equal-length requested-unit windows; arithmetic decomposition, not evidence of individual customer switching.

result.warehouse_scope: Supplier receipts and expected arrivals cover shared warehouse products; they are not district-specific stock.

result.name: Value price · Strawberry · Water-based
result.effect_basis: Estimated sustained change in requested/forecast ratio from baseline to recent, after shrinkage; not the raw recent requested-minus-forecast percentage.
result.series_scope: Observed requests and current-model expectations for eligible SKU/district units; SKU promotion days excluded. Observed chart values are not winsorised.
result.pallet_change_basis: Footprint of the change in total purchased cases; not a change in simultaneous warehouse peak occupancy.
result.peak_capacity_scope: Whole warehouse with ALL cohort adjustments and current overrides already included together.

leaf.series_scope: Observed requests and current-model expectations for eligible SKU/district units; SKU promotion days excluded. Observed chart values are not winsorised.

trace.tree: inverse-variance conditional inference; max depth 3; min 3 distinct SKUs per child
trace.permutation_scheme: product tags: whole SKU district vectors within equal-support strata; district tags: districts within each SKU; y and v paired; max across all candidates
trace.sku_covariance: district demand weights; conditional variances independent; shared leaf posterior covariance
trace.unit_definition: SKU × district; complete observed and issued rows; at least one eligible day in each window
trace.winsorisation: per store/SKU 99th percentile across eligible 70-day history before aggregation
trace.overdispersion: sample variance of seven-day (A-E)/sqrt(E) baseline residuals, floored at 1
trace.forecast_error_variance: Per SKU/district, sample variance of eligible baseline seven-day log((A+0.5)/(E+0.5)) current-model residuals minus mean 1/(E+0.5) count-sampling variance, clipped at zero; log-rate units squared. Add this weekly systematic variance times (7/recent eligible days + 1/baseline eligible weeks) to each unit log-change variance. Uses historical issued weather and baseline outcomes only; part of the baseline may be in the current model training period. No percentage floor.
trace.drilldown_effect: Inverse-variance weighted mean unit log change transformed with expm1 × 100 at each actual tree prefix, before leaf and SKU shrinkage. Daily requests are raw eligible observations; siblings are within the same parent.

method.order_impact_scope: SKU order differences allocated by each leaf district forecast share; case total rounded. Disjoint district leaves do not duplicate total value.
method.value_method: Normal expected shortage difference under the adjusted demand distribution
